full_judgment: 3. Mr Lokman Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned Joint District Judge after considering the facts and circumstances of the case rightly held that the questions of limitation and res judicata are mixed question of law and facts; therefore, without taking evidence, the plaint cannot be rejected; but unfortunately, the learned Additional District Judge without converting the finding of the learned Joint District Judge struck down the order of the learned Joint District Judge and, as such, committed an error of law causing serious failure of justice; therefore, the same is liable to be interfered with by this Court. He further submits that the relief sought in earlier suit and the instant suit, which are distinct from each other; therefore, the present suit is not barred by res judicata. He next submits that the plea of res judicata can be decided upon taking evidence only but not by invoking Order 7 Rule 11 of the CPC. In support of his submission, he relies on the decision of case of Mahbubul Hague vs Md A Kader Munshi, reported in 52 DLR (AD) 49, Sreemati Pushpa Rani Das vs AKM Habibur Rahman & others, reported in 1993 BLD (AD) 217 and Rabija Khatun & others vs Badsha Meah & others, reported in 1995 BLD 325 = 47 DLR 511.
